topic.angle: A famous idea that struggled to replicate

card.title: The willpower muscle that didn't replicate

panels.text: Ego depletion is the idea that self-control draws on mental resources that can be used up, leaving less for the next task.
Roy Baumeister and colleagues proposed that self-control works like a muscle that can tire. Later experiments seemed to support the model.
Then came a big test. In 2016, a multi-lab replication study with 2141 participants at two dozen labs, using one protocol, failed to find any evidence for ego depletion.

Baumeister and Vohs objected to the protocol used. A later 36-lab replication led by Vohs, with 3531 participants, also found no effect. The lesson: one famous result is not settled until independent labs reproduce it.

probes.question: What is ego depletion?
options: Having too high an opinion of yourself
The idea that self-control draws on a limited resource that can be used up

probes.question: True or false: a 2016 multi-lab replication failed to find evidence for ego depletion.

claims.quote: Later experimental findings showed support for this muscle model of self-control and ego depletion.
